newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Sept 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to a report commissioned by the Australian Financial Markets Association, Australia's push to establish itself as a major financial centre for Asian markets has not been successful, with the combined annual turnover of the over-the-counter market, the Sydney Futures Exchange and the Australian Stock Exchange falling by A$1 trillion in 1995-96 to A$24 trillion. Page 1.

Ahead of its demutualisation and stock exchange listing Colonial Mutual will inject A$150 million into its banking arm as part of a A$550 million capital raising exercise. The State Bank of New South Wales will use the funds and is expected to be relaunched today as Colonial State Bank. Page 1.

Using questionnaires and random visits, the Insurance and Superannuation Commission will investigate the level of compliance with the law among 130,000 small superannuation trusts. The job is to be carried out on "excluded funds" - funds with five or fewer than five members. Page 3.

The Federal Treasury may have put many listed companies out of pocket, as it has postponed the implementation date for new CGT provisions that require companies to test their share registers for a change in ownership until January 20, after telling the companies the Budget deadline was September 20. Pg 3.

When digital satellite broadcasting becomes unfettered from July next year, providing the opportunity for many international telecoms such as AT&T to enter the market, people within the industry like Rupert Murdoch and Kerry Stokes believe it will become larger than the Internet. Page 19.

James Hardie Industries Ltd has sealed a deal to sell-off its US-based global irrigation business for A$165 million to The Toro Company. James Hardie only expected an amount of between A$126 and A$150 million on the sale. Pg 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The head of the Royal Dutch Shell group, Cornelius Herkstroter, has predicted a group of multinational companies - Mobil, Texaco, Exxon, BP, Shell, Chevron, BHP Petroleum and Woodside Petroleum - will jointly develop their interests in natural gas reserve in the North West Shelf project, off the West Australian coast. Page 29.

BHP investors should brace themselves for a marathon annual general meeting tomorrow, with complaints expected to be aired on topics like the 23 percent fall in the group's September quarter net profit, its weak share price and problems in its steel and copper operations. Page 29.

Australian Gas Association chairman Greg Harvey, who is also Gas & Fuel in Victoria managing director, has criticised the State and Federal Governments over their role in the creation of a national gas market, saying the gas industry had gone as far as it could in the reform process without the Government clarifying certain issues. Page 29.

The impending introduction of the Federal Government's "rule off the books" legislation applying to privatisations, means the Queensland Government's mega-merger of Suncorp Insurance & Finance, the Queensland Industry Development Corp and Metway Bank Ltd stands to gain at least a A$40 million tax windfall. Page 31.

TNT Ltd managing director David Mortimer said yesterday even though the company still believed its share price would recover enough to allow the shares to convert normally between November and May, it was still looking at extending the life of its convertble preference shares or buying them back to avoid a massive dilution of TNT's stock. Page 31.

Senior Federal officials met leading business figures in Canberra last week to begin preparing a strategy to take to the Singapore ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation in December, deciding to back moves to bring competition policy within the ambit of world trade negotiations. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The executive director of MIM's Mount Isa operations, Phil Wright, has conceded that Mount Isa is expected to run up substantial losses in the current year due to the plunge in the copper price and the continuing strength of the Australian dollar. Wright aid the losses were expected despite dramatic improvements in management and work practices since last year's lock out. Page 35.

Following BHP's disastrous 22.8 percent slump in first quarter profits, chief executive John Prescott admitted yesterday the group would have to make adjustments to cope with the lower copper price as the outlook in that area was bleak and could cast a shadow over long-term earnings growth. Page 35.

Ahead of an international roadshow campaign to promote Optus Communications to institutions, the telecommunications group's board will meet today to sign-off on the group's A$4.5 billion sharemarket listing. A registered prospectus for the public offering is expected to be released in late October. Page 35.

Australian financial markets will be on edge in the early part of the week awaiting the results of the US Federal Reserve meeting on Wednesday, which is tipped to lift interest rates 0.25 percent in a bid to pre-empt a jump in inflation. Page 37.

The price war that was expected to occur after Franklins slashed prices in South Australia to recapture market share from Woolworths and Coles Myer's Bi-Lo stores has been averted after Woolworths launched a pre-emptive strike by taking up to 20 and 30 percent off a selection of its home brands for one week from September 9. Page 37.

In what is being seen as the first step by the Colonial Group, which purchased the State Bank in 1994, aimed at cutting costs and increasing return on assets employed within the next two years, the State Bank will unveil a new name and corporate identity today. Page 37.
THE AGE

Despite improvements to its management and work practices since last year's lock-out, MIM Holdings yesterday admitted that due to the plunging price of copper its Mount Isa operations were expected to run substantial loses in the present year. Page C1.

BHP chief executive John Prescott stated yesterday that with the falling price of copper its new copper arm would have to focus on costs and efficiency and further improvement in the performance of BHP's other mines would have to be made. Page C1.

Another strong jump in annual national sales has once again shown the strength of Australia's natural gas market. Domestic sales have increased by eight percent in the last year and 30 percent over the last five. Page C2.

There is doubt amongst the key participants in the North West Shelf gas project over whether there is enough of a reserve base for a A$6.8 billion expansion of the facility. Shell Australia stated on Friday that the project still had to prove that it did have the gas reserves necessary for an expansion of this size. Page C2.

Within three weeks Australia's second biggest life office, National Mutual Holdings, will be placed on the stock exchange and by the middle of next year Melbourne-based Colonial Group will join it. Analysts predict a market capitalisation of up to A$15 bilion in what, at the moment, is a non existent market on the stock exchange. Page C3.
Vespa, the company that makes trendy motor-scooters, will enter a new market by selling clothes and accessories bearing the Vespa trademark, in the hope of harnessing a cult wearer market. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
